title: bd hook integration bypasses project pre-commit (core.hooksPath conflict)
description:
bd's hook integration sets `core.hooksPath` to `.beads/hooks/` so its own pre-commit/post-checkout/etc. wrappers run. Side effect: Git never looks at `.git/hooks/`, so the project's pre-commit hook (`.git-hooks/pre-commit`, installed by `make setup` into `.git/hooks/`) is silently bypassed.

This is the project's Prettier gate (`make autofix && make check`). Without it, formatting drift slips through commits and only CI catches it (see PR #29 where `.claude/settings.json` was missing a trailing newline).

## Options to consider

1. **Chain hooks**: append the project's pre-commit logic AFTER bd's BEGIN/END markers in `.beads/hooks/pre-commit`. `make setup` would need to know how to integrate (idempotent insert after the bd-managed block).
2. **Use bd's hook config to call out**: `bd hooks add pre-commit` if such a thing exists, registering the project hook through bd.
3. **Drop `core.hooksPath` and let bd hooks live as wrappers in `.git/hooks/`**: less integrated with bd but restores Git's default lookup so project hooks coexist.

Affects every commit made in any worktree (worktrees inherit `core.hooksPath` from the main repo). Spotted while addressing a review comment on PR #29.

title: Add kix:triage skill to categorize bd todo items
description:
Add a `kix:triage` skill that walks `bd todo` and categorizes every item as
one of `bug`, `feature`, `chore`, or `epic`, applying type + priority so items
leave `bd todo`.

## Epic handling

Three cases the skill must cover:

1. **Promote single task to epic.** A task that's actually big enough to
   break into multiple sub-tasks becomes an epic itself.
2. **Create new epic from a group.** Several related tasks where it makes
   sense to introduce a new epic and group them under it. The skill creates
   the epic and links the tasks.
3. **Slot under existing epic.** A task that fits inside an open or
   in-progress epic gets a normal type (bug/feature/chore) and a dependency
   link to that epic — not promoted to epic itself.

## Interaction model

- Do not ask one item at a time blind. First reason through all proposed
  movements (types, priorities, epic groupings, links) for the whole
  `bd todo` list.
- Present the full plan in a digestible overview so the user can see the
  shape before committing.
- Then walk through decisions step by step — task-by-task, or
  group-by-group when items cluster — letting the user accept, override, or
  skip each.
- Apply changes via `bd update` / `bd create` / `bd dep add` as confirmed.

## Acceptance

- After running the skill, every previously-listed `bd todo` item either:
  - has a non-task type (bug/feature/chore) and a priority, OR
  - has been promoted to `epic`, OR
  - has been closed.
- New epics created during triage are properly linked to the tasks they
  group.
- Tasks slotted under existing epics have a dependency on the epic.
- Skill ships at `claude-code/skills/triage/SKILL.md` so it surfaces as
  `/kix:triage` and propagates wherever the kix plugin is installed.

title: Add kix:commit-msg skill for git hook message generation
description:
Extract commit message generation from `kix:commit` into a standalone `kix:commit-msg` skill, invoked by a per-repo `prepare-commit-msg` git hook. Each repo opts in and configures the hook to its own preferences (message format, references to repo-specific guidance like AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md "Commit message" sections).

After this, both bare `git commit` and `kix:commit` produce repo-conformant messages through the same path: the hook runs `kix:commit-msg`, which generates the message based on the staged diff plus any user-provided context.

The existing `kix:commit` skill stops generating the message itself and instead calls `git commit -m "<context>"`, letting the hook take over. It keeps the lifecycle logic that doesn't belong in a per-commit hook: staging strategy, auto-fix loop, resume state, stash handling.
design:
## Empirical basis

Tested in a sandbox repo: `prepare-commit-msg` runs for ALL commits including `git commit -m`, and is NOT suppressed by `--no-verify`. Whether `-m` "wins" is entirely up to the hook script — git does no auto-suppression. The hook receives positional args: `$1` = msg file path, `$2` = source, `$3` = commit SHA (for `-c`/`-C`/`--amend`).

## Hook behavior matrix (branches on `$2`)

| `$2` value | Trigger | Hook action |
|---|---|---|
| `message` | `-m` or `-F` used | Treat the `-m` value as **user context**, not the final message. Pass to skill as context; skill generates the proper message. |
| `template` | `commit.template` set | Generate, replacing template. |
| `merge` | merge commit | Skip — git's merge message is canonical. |
| `squash` | squash | Skip. |
| `commit` | `-c` / `-C` / `--amend` | Skip — preserve the borrowed message. |
| empty | bare `git commit` | Generate fresh; editor opens with result. |

## Opt-out

Hook should honor an env var (e.g. `KIX_SKIP_MSG=1`) so users can bypass per-commit when they truly want their `-m` text verbatim. `--no-verify` does NOT bypass `prepare-commit-msg`, so this is the only escape hatch.

## kix:commit-msg skill inputs

Hook shells out to `claude` invoking `kix:commit-msg`, passing:
- path to the message file (so the skill writes the result there)
- source `$2` (so the skill knows whether to skip)
- the staged diff
- user-provided context (the original `$1` contents when `$2 == "message"`)
- pointer to repo-specific guidance (AGENTS.md / CLAUDE.md "Commit message" section, or a dedicated file the repo configures)

## kix:commit skill changes

Currently generates the message inline (Step 3). After this work:
- Drop Step 3 message generation.
- Step 5 calls `git commit -m "<context from $ARGUMENTS>"` (or bare `git commit` if no context).
- The installed hook + `kix:commit-msg` produce the actual message.
- Keep: staging strategy (Step 1), auto-fix loop (Step 6), resume state, stash handling (Step 7).

## Open questions

- Does the hook shell out to `claude` synchronously (blocks the commit, needs auth/network) or stage a placeholder for an out-of-band agent? Synchronous is simpler and matches user intent ("git commit produces a good message"); accept the latency cost.
- Ship a default hook template under `claude-code/templates/` or a separate `hooks/` dir? Repos copy or symlink it during setup.

title: Per-kind Task body templates from .github issue templates
description:
Replace the single `claude-code/templates/task.md` with four per-kind Task body
templates, copied verbatim in shape from the GitHub issue templates in
`0k-software/.github`:

- `task-feature.md` — from `.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/2-feature.yml` (✨ Feature,
  including the Pre-flight checklist)
- `task-chore.md` — from `.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/3-task.yml` (🛠️ Task in
  `.github`; renamed Chore here so it doesn't collide with the Kix Task entity)
- `task-bug.md` — from `.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/4-bug.yml` (🐛 Bug, including
  Severity)
- `task-enhancement.md` — from `.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/5-enhancement.yml` (🧱
  Enhancement)

Each rendered Task body should match what the corresponding GitHub issue
template produces when submitted — same section labels, same default values.

`kix:create-task` should pick which of the four templates to stamp out by
**inferring the kind from the user's context** rather than from an explicit
flag. Two signals to consider, in order:

1. The framing/free-text the user wrote after the command invocation (e.g. "fix
   the flaky login test" → `bug`; "make the dashboard load faster" →
   `enhancement`).
2. The parent Pitch's title and Summary, when `--pitch <id>` is given (e.g. a
   Pitch titled "Auth modernization" with feature-shaped Summary → `feature`).

If both signals are absent or ambiguous, fall back to a sensible default
(probably `chore`) and state the inferred kind in the confirmation output so
the user can correct it.

## Resolution

Implemented on branch `kix/21-task-kind-templates`. Added the four per-kind
Task body templates (`task-feature.md`, `task-chore.md`, `task-bug.md`,
`task-enhancement.md`) ported from `0k-software/.github`'s issue templates,
removed the generic `task.md`, and extended `kix:create-task` with a new "Infer
the Task kind" step that picks the template from framing text / parent Pitch /
seed Requests with `chore` as the fallback and echoes the inferred kind in the
confirmation. PR: https://github.com/0k-software/kix-agents/pull/20

description:
# Outcome subfolders instead of front-matter field

Instead of an `outcome` field in the Request front-matter, store the outcome by
location: a subfolder per outcome. New Requests land in `inbox/`. Triage moves
the file into the matching outcome folder.

Folders:

- `.kix/requests/inbox/` — outcome not yet decided (current Inbox view)
- `.kix/requests/postponed/`
- `.kix/requests/linked/`
- `.kix/requests/closed/`

This makes the on-disk layout match the Inbox/triage mental model and lets
users see counts at a glance with `ls`. Open question: whether `linked_to` also
moves to a folder convention or stays as front-matter.

## Resolution

Shipped in:

- [813c732](https://github.com/0k-software/kix/commit/813c732) — feat: encode
  Request outcome by subfolder (Request 9)

`linked_to` stayed in front-matter — encoding the target Pitch/Task as a nested
folder would have broken the `ls`-count goal and the symmetry with the other
outcomes.

title: Warn on vague Request bodies during creation
description:
# Warn on vague Request bodies during creation

Request creation should stay rough and friction-free, but very terse briefs can
be hard to grasp later — see `.kix/requests/4-create-pitch-skill.md`, which
gives no hint of what the skill is for. When the brief is too thin to infer
meaning, the `/kix:request` skill should still create the Request, but warn the
user that the body is vague and more context would help future triagers.

## Resolution

Implemented on branch `claude/implement-feature-8-6vLVd`. Extended the
`kix:create-request` skill's confirm step with a soft vagueness check: when the
body is empty or too thin to convey area/outcome/motivation, the skill now
prints a warning alongside the file path. Creation itself stays friction-free —
the warning is a nudge, not a rejection. Added a matching `### Changed` entry
to the Unreleased section of CHANGELOG.md.

title: `create-pitch` skill
description:
# `create-pitch` skill

Add a `create-pitch` skill that creates a Pitch from one or more existing
Requests. Input: a Request id/link, multiple Request ids/links, or Request
ids/links plus framing instructions about what the Pitch is about (e.g. a
bug-bashing batch).

- **Single Request, no extra framing** — infer the Pitch is about that one
  Request. Seed the Summary from it directly.
- **Multiple Requests, or any framing instructions alongside the id(s)** —
  treat it as a grouped Pitch (e.g. a bug bash, a theme). The Summary should
  reflect the group/theme, with each source Request copied in.

Pitches need a template (default format) — create that too as part of this
work. When the skill runs, it instantiates the template, references the source
Request(s) (via `linked_to` or equivalent — supporting multiple links), and
copies the known info into a **Summary** section at the top of the Pitch.

**Do not refine or shape the Pitch during creation** — no AI or human time
spent rewording. Refinement is a separate, later step. This skill is called
during triage, and triage must be fast.

## Resolution

title: Skill to implement requests via branch and PR
description:
# Skill to implement requests via branch and PR

Add a new skill (`kix:implement` or similar) that automates the implementation
workflow for a plain request. The skill should:

1. Open a git branch scoped to the request.
2. Implement what's requested, splitting work across multiple commits to make
   review easier.
3. Mark the request as closed (move it to `closed/`) within that branch.
4. Open a pull request when the work is done.

Initially, the skill should be able to operate directly on top of a plain
Request (no pitch or plan required), so the team can move quickly before the
full Kix process is in place.

the other entity types.

Open questions: input shape (id alone, or id + reason?); whether the rules
differ enough between entity types to warrant separate `/close-request`,
`/close-pitch`, `/close-task` skills, or one polymorphic `/close` that infers
the type from the id.

## Resolution

Implemented on branch `claude/implement-feature-13-Noa1M`. The skill landed as
`kix:cancel` rather than `kix:close` after PR review — it turned out the
operation is fundamentally about cancellation (discarding work), not about
moving to a finished terminal state. `/cancel <id> [reason]`
(`claude-code/commands/cancel.md`) identifies the entity by globbing
`.kix/{requests,pitches/<id>-*/,pitches/*/tasks/<id>-*/}` and applies the
type-specific cancellation: Requests move to `.kix/requests/closed/` with the
reason in the `## Resolution` body; Pitches and Tasks get a `cancelled_at`
timestamp added to front-matter while `phase:` is preserved (so the phase the
work was in at cancellation is part of the record). Cancellation is orthogonal
to phase progression. No cascade on linked Requests when a Pitch is cancelled —
they are reported in the confirmation so the user can decide. PR:
https://github.com/0k-software/kix-agents/pull/17

title: Drop the type field from Request front-matter
description:
# Drop the type field from Request front-matter

The `type: request` field in Request front-matter is redundant — files under
`.kix/requests/` are Requests by location. Remove the field from the schema and
from the `/kix:request` skill template.

## Resolution

Implemented on branch `claude/implement-feature-10-LhGDH`. Removed
`type: request` from the `kix:create-request` skill template and stripped the
field from existing Request files. PR:
https://github.com/0k-software/kix-agents/pull/16

title: Rename `request` skill or add aliases
description:
# Rename `request` skill or add aliases

Should `request` be renamed? Candidates: `capture`, `create`, `new`. Or keep
`request` as the canonical name (e.g. `kix:create-request`) and expose multiple
aliases pointing at it.

title: Why use `commands/` folder instead of skills
description:
# Why use `commands/` folder instead of skills

Why are we using a `commands/` folder instead of skills?

title: Natural-language "commit" should trigger the Kix commit skill
description:
# Natural-language "commit" should trigger the Kix commit skill

When I say "commit" or "commit this" without typing `/kix:commit`, Claude
should still route through the Kix commit flow. Suspicion: defining these as
slash commands doesn't support natural-language triggering — they should be
skills instead, so intent alone activates them.

title: ID conflicts when multiple people allocate IDs in parallel
description:
# ID conflicts when multiple people allocate IDs in parallel

The current ID allocator reads `.kix/.state/next-id` and increments it. In a
team setting this collides: if I create a Request locally and don't push, and
someone else also creates one on their branch, both end up with the same ID. We
need a strategy that survives parallel work across branches and people.
close_reason: We are using beads now, not needed anymore

title: Route Request/Pitch/Task creation through Kix CLI
description:
# Route Request/Pitch/Task creation through Kix CLI

Eventually, all creations of Requests, Pitches, and Tasks should go through the
Kix CLI rather than being written directly by a skill. That gives us a place to
enforce consistency checks and invariants so creation is deterministic instead
of stochastic.
close_reason: Superseded by beads migration: 'bd' is now the canonical CLI for Request/Pitch/Task creation, replacing the planned Kix CLI. Consistency checks and invariants belong in beads workflows.

title: `triage` skill
description:
# `triage` skill

Add a `triage` skill that delegates to `create-task` and `create-pitch` to
produce the linked downstream artifact for a Request.
close_reason: Superseded by beads migration: create-task/create-pitch skills are being retired (kxa-s4r), so a triage skill that delegates to them is no longer the right shape. Triage now happens via 'bd ready' / 'bd update --claim'.

title: link-pitch and link-task skills for existing entities
description:
# link-pitch and link-task skills for existing entities

Add `link-pitch` and `link-task` skills that link an existing Request to an
existing Pitch or Task — counterparts to `create-pitch` / `create-task`, which
create a new entity from a Request. Useful when a Request turns out to be the
same problem as a Pitch/Task already in flight, or when grouping late-arriving
Requests under an existing initiative.

Inputs roughly: a Request id and a target Pitch/Task id. The skill updates the
Request's `outcome: linked` and `linked_to: <target_id>`, and (for Pitches)
appends the Request id to the target's `requests:` front-matter list. Mirror
the validation rules from `create-pitch` (already-linked warning, missing-id
abort).
close_reason: Superseded by beads migration: depended on .kix file-based frontmatter (outcome: linked, linked_to:) and create-pitch/create-task skills, all retired. Linking now happens via 'bd dep add' between bd issues.

title: Re-audit phxagents (claude-elixir-phoenix) when v3.0.0 ships
description: The kxa-9oh security audit covered v2.8.8 and was clean, but it's point-in-time. v3.0.0 adds Codex/OpenCode/Pi multi-agent support — review the new hooks, agent prompts, and any new MCP/network surface before bumping the pinned version. Blocked until v3.0.0 is released.

title: Optional backprop hook on bd close (Cave Kit inspiration, per kxa-eal)
description: From kxa-eal: Cave Kit's backprop loop turns bug fixes into persistent invariants. Optional kix-agents adaptation: on `bd close` of a bug-type issue, prompt to add the lesson as an acceptance rule on the parent epic. Could be implemented as a small bd hook or a /kix:backprop skill.\n\nLow priority — useful but not blocking anything.

title: Adopt living SPEC.md + bd convention (Cave Kit inspiration, per kxa-eal)
description: From kxa-eal: Cave Kit's single living SPEC.md per project is a useful pattern. Bd already stores §T (tasks) and §B (bugs); a SPEC.md could store §G (goal) / §C (constraints) / §I (interfaces) / §V (invariants) as a stable architectural record per project. Investigate adopting this convention in kix-agents itself (and potentially as a /kix:spec skill that wraps the pattern).\n\nNot a Cave Kit dependency — just the idea. Caveman encoding optional.

title: Per-project phxagents adoption for Elixir/Phoenix work (per kxa-9oh)
description: Security audit on oliver-kriska/claude-elixir-phoenix v2.8.8 passed (see docs/kix/kxa-9oh/spec.md §security review). Adoption plan: install per-project on developer machines that work on Elixir/Phoenix code. Pair with the workflow plugin (superpowers per kxa-tts) — use /phx:plan + /phx:work + /phx:review as domain helpers inside the workflow, NOT /phx:full. Pin to a known-good tag rather than tracking main.\n\nThis issue is the decision-tracking record; the actual install is a per-developer action on Elixir/Phoenix projects, not a kix-agents repo change.

title: Document optional caveman install for kix-agents contributors (per kxa-x83)
description: Add a short section to docs/kix-agents.md (or contributor notes) describing the optional caveman install for this repo. Mention default mode is 'full', the per-session /caveman command for switching, and that code blocks / commits / PR descriptions are always written normally regardless of caveman mode. Don't enforce on consumers — per-developer preference.

value: Do not close a beads issue right after opening its PR. Mark it in_progress and link the PR (e.g. via --notes) — only close after the PR merges. Why: PR review can change scope, request rework, or get rejected; closing prematurely loses the work-tracking signal. How to apply: in any kix:implement / branch-and-PR flow, after pushing the PR set status=in_progress + add the PR URL via bd update --notes; defer bd close until merge.
